## What is STAC?

STAC - **SpatioTemporal Asset Catalogs** is a API where data providers implement a structured access to their products.


Tutorial tutorial is heavily inspired (i.e. copied and adapted) from:

- [https://stacspec.org/en/tutorials/1-download-data-using-r/](https://stacspec.org/en/tutorials/1-download-data-using-r/)
- [https://appelmar.github.io/ogh2021/tutorial.html#Introduction](https://appelmar.github.io/ogh2021/tutorial.html#Introduction)

```{r}
#| label: packages

# install.packages("rstac")
# install.packages("sf")
# install.packages("terra")
# install.packages("tidyverse")
# install.packages("gdalcubes")
# install.packages("mapview")

library(sf)
library(terra)
library(rstac)
library(tidyverse)
library(gdalcubes)
library(mapview)
mapviewOptions(basemaps = "OpenStreetMap")
```

In order to query satellite data, we need to define a spatial extent and the time range we want data from.

```{r}
#| label: area of interests

aoi <- st_read("data/aoi/aoi_goreangab.geojson")
mapview(aoi, col.regions = "white", color = "black", alpha = 1)

# specific format for bounding box and time
aoi_bbox <- aoi |> st_bbox() |> as.vector()
timespan <- "2025-05-01T00:00:00Z/2025-05-30T23:59:59Z"
```



## rstac and gdalcubes


### Microsoft Planetary Computer

Stac Collection of the Microsoft Planetary Computer: [https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/catalog](https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/catalog)

```{r}
#| label: Microsoft Collections

stac_source <- rstac::stac(
  "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/"
)


rstac::get_request(stac_source)

collections_query <- stac_source |>
  rstac::collections()

collections_query
available_collections <- rstac::get_request(collections_query)
available_collections$collections


```



- Example data: Harmonised Landsat Sentinel 2 (hls) to get Sentinel data in 30m spatial resolution
- [https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/dataset/hls2-s30](https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/dataset/hls2-s30)


```{r}
#| label: Microsoft S2


items <- rstac::stac_search(
  q = stac_source,
  collections = "hls2-s30",
  datetime = "2025-05-01/2025-05-30",
  bbox = aoi_bbox,
  limit = 30
) |> ext_query("eo:cloud_cover" < 80)
items = post_request(items)
items

items <- items_sign_planetary_computer(items)

```



```{r}
#| label: explore items

items_datetime(items)
items_bbox(items)
items_assets(items)
```



## Create the actual image collection from the items

```{r}
#| label: Stac Image Collection


wanted_assets = items_assets(items)[1:14]

collection_s2 = stac_image_collection(items$features, asset_names = wanted_assets)
collection_s2

```



## gdalcubes to access only the aoi


- UTM Zone of Namibia is 33S, EPSG:32733
- Here we define a data_cube. Think of it like an empty template where we put data in.

```{r}
#| label: gdalcubes datacube definition


cube_box <- aoi |> st_transform(32733) |> st_bbox()

spatiotemporal_extent <- list(
  t0 = "2025-05-01",
  t1 = "2025-05-30",
  left = cube_box["xmin"],
  right = cube_box["xmax"],
  bottom = cube_box["ymin"],
  top = cube_box["ymax"]
)


v <- gdalcubes::cube_view(
  srs = "EPSG:32733",
  extent = spatiotemporal_extent,
  dx = 30,
  dy = 30,
  dt = "P1D",
  aggregation = "first",
  resampling = "near"
)
v


```



```{r}
#| label: download the cube

cu = raster_cube(collection_s2, v)
cu
```


### Output

Here we write out the individual composites


```{r}
#| label: writeOut
#| eval: FALSE

acq_dates = items_datetime(items) |> substr(1, 10) |>
  unique() |>
  sort()


dir.create("temp")
# write the time slices with actual images out
for (d in acq_dates) {
  cu |>
    slice_time(datetime = d) |>
    write_tif(dir = "temp/", prefix = "HLS_S30_", COG = TRUE)
}
```
